DeepWalk can be viewed as a special case of node2vec because node2vec generalizes the random-walk sampling strategy used by DeepWalk. In node2vec, the next step of a walk is chosen using a biased second-order transition rule controlled by the return parameter p and the in-out parameter q. When p=1 and q=1, those bias terms disappear, so the transition probabilities reduce to an unbiased first-order random walk in which each neighbor is sampled uniformly according to the graph adjacency structure. That is exactly the walk-generation mechanism used by DeepWalk.

Equivalently, node2vec with p=1 and q=1 preserves the same context-sampling behavior as DeepWalk: it generates random walks from each source node and then treats nodes appearing within a fixed window on those walks as training contexts for the skip-gram objective. Since the walk process is no longer biased toward breadth-first or depth-first exploration, the resulting training data distribution matches DeepWalk’s. Therefore, DeepWalk is the p=1, q=1 instance of node2vec, differing only in that node2vec was designed to allow biased walks when p and q are not both 1.
confidence_reasoning: This is a standard equivalence in the node2vec/DeepWalk literature, and the parameter setting p=q=1 directly removes node2vec's walk bias, yielding DeepWalk's unbiased random walks.
